title: As a power user, the agent operates a real phone (tap, swipe, type) to finish a task I describe in plain language
As a power user, the agent operates desktop applications (click, type, keyboard shortcuts) across the whole OS, not one walled app
As a developer, the control path (USB HID, accessibility APIs, OS input events) is documented, so I know how inputs reach the device
As a developer, the same agent targets more than one OS (macOS, Windows, Linux, or mobile) with documented per-target support
As an AI-native user, the agent perceives the live screen (capture or vision input) and grounds its actions on what is actually displayed
As a developer, the approach to locating UI elements (accessibility tree, OCR, set-of-marks, coordinates) is documented, so misclicks are debuggable
As a power user, a multi-step task that crosses several apps completes without me babysitting every step
As a developer, the agent recovers from popups, state drift, and failed actions with documented retry behavior instead of wedging
As an AI-native user, the vendor publishes task-completion benchmark results (OSWorld or similar) with enough detail to reproduce them
As a developer, I get from install to a first completed device task using the quickstart docs alone
As a power user, hardware rigs come with a bill of materials, wiring, and flashing steps I can follow end to end
As a developer, I can run the agent against a sandboxed VM or container before pointing it at a real device
As an operator, sensitive actions (payments, sends, deletes) pause for my approval before the agent executes them
As an operator, I can limit which apps, surfaces, or accounts the agent may touch, and the limit is enforced, not advisory
As an operator, the agent can work behind logins without my credentials passing through the model or its logs
As a developer, I can point the agent at my own model endpoint (OpenAI-compatible or otherwise) through documented configuration
As a power user, the agent runs with a local model, so device control does not depend on a cloud API
As an operator, every run is reviewable afterwards: the steps taken, the screens seen, and the inputs injected
As an operator, per-run metrics (success, duration, token or dollar cost) are reported, so I can compare runs
As a developer, I can embed device control in my own application through a documented SDK or API
As a power user, I can schedule a device task or trigger it from an external event, not only run it interactively
